histories.MatterHistoryActionText: Upon motion duly seconded, the bill passed first reading and will be considered at the next regular meeting. The bill is referred to the Budget and Finance Committee and the Planning and Zoning Committee.

The bill was approved by the Budget and Finance Committee and the Planning and Zoning Committee. Council Member Capp moved that the bill be deferred to the November 5, 2026 Council meeting and to hold a public hearing on the bill, which motion was seconded and approved by a voice vote of the Council.

matter.MatterTitle: An ordinance approving Amendment No. 3 to the East Bank Redevelopment Plan.

text:
..title
An ordinance approving Amendment No. 3 to the East Bank Redevelopment Plan.
..body
WHEREAS, the original East Bank Redevelopment Plan was enacted by Ordinance No. BL096-163 in 1996 to facilitate the construction of an NFL football stadium; and 
WHEREAS, the Project Area was extended in 1999 by Ordinance No. BL099-1647 to include properties on and in the vicinity of Main Street and Woodland Street; and 
WHEREAS, Amendment 2 to the East Bank Redevelopment Plan was enacted by Ordinance No. BL2025-1104 in 2025 and consisted of certain changes to the text, boundaries, and maps of the East Bank Redevelopment Plan; and
WHEREAS, the existing East Bank Redevelopment Plan expires December 31, 2026; and 
WHEREAS, there is a desire to extend the land use controls contained in the East Bank Redevelopment Plan through December 31, 2031, to permit additional time for consideration of a Transit Oriented Redevelopment District. 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ENACTED BY THE COUNCIL OF THE METROPOLITAN GOVERNMENT OF NASHVILLE AND DAVIDSON COUNTY: 
Section 1. That the findings and determinations relative to the “East Bank Redevelopment Plan” are hereby reaffirmed and redetermined. 
Section 2. The final paragraph of Section A of the Plan is deleted in its entirety and replaced with the following: “A review of the Main Street corridor in 2026 indicated that the presence of blight remained in this transit corridor. The duration of the Redevelopment Plan should be extended for five years to December 31, 2031, as plans progress on transitioning the area to a Transit Oriented Redevelopment District.”
Section 3. That Paragraph 2.d. Period of Duration of These Provisions is deleted in its entirety and replaced with the following: “The provisions of this Plan, specifying the land uses for the Project Area and the requirements and restrictions with respect thereto, shall commence upon approval of the Plan by the governing body of the Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County, and shall continue in effect until December 31, 2031.”
Section 4. This ordinance shall take effect on December 31, 2026, after its enactment, the welfare of The Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County requiring it.
..Agenda Analysis
Analysis

This ordinance approves the second amendment to the East Bank Redevelopment Plan, as managed by the Metropolitan Housing and Development Agency. The ordinance would replace the text of the East Bank Redevelopment Plan and include new maps and descriptions of the project boundaries.

The original East Bank Redevelopment Plan was enacted by Ordinance No. BL96-163 in 1996 to facilitate the construction of a professional football stadium. The project area was extended in 1999 by Ordinance No. BL99-1647 to include properties on and in the vicinity of Main Street and Woodland Street in East Nashville.

The second amendment to this redevelopment plan reduced the size of the project area of the East Bank Redevelopment Plan and extended the duration of the plan until December 31, 2026. The amendment would remove the part of the project area west of the Interstate 65/24 loop from the redevelopment plan. The portions of the project area east of the interstate loop would remain in the redevelopment plan until December 31, 2026. 

The proposed amendment would extend the duration of the redevelopment plan for five additional years until December 31, 2031. The extension will allow for time to consider the creation of a Transit Oriented Development District.

The MDHA Board of Commissioners approved this amendment at its September 8, 2026, meeting.
